title: Judicial Review, Fundamental Rights, and the Invisible Constitution

sections.title: The Structural Mechanism
sections.content: Following the 1989 regime change, the Hungarian Constitutional Court under President László Sólyom became one of the most powerful constitutional courts in the world. Its hallmark was the 'actio popularis': anyone could challenge any law without proving personal standing.

sections.title: Rhetorical Application & Stance
sections.content: Sólyom coined the doctrine of the *láthatatlan alkotmány* (invisible constitution): the idea that constitutional adjudication must follow a coherent, morally grounded system of fundamental principles that transcends the literal text of the written constitution.
